entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Kept alive almost entirely by *Jabberwocky*; it sounds invented, because it nearly is.
examples: Come to my arms, my beamish boy!

entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: The British phrasing of the same brief, unloaded glance.

entries.definition: given to gross intemperance in eating or drinking
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Formal and disgusted, and about drink as much as food.

entries.definition: very good; of the highest quality
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Unqualified praise - at the top of its class.

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The adverb of *stingy*: the plain word. Its mirror image is *thrifty*, which praises the identical behaviour.

entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Closest to neutral here - a condition met rather than a character described.

entries.definition: in an idle and lackadaisical manner
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The adverb of *lackadaisical*: comic rather than damning; the failing is a lack of spirit, not of will.
examples: he was hanging around the house lackadaisically

entries.definition: devouring or craving food in great quantities
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Rare enough to sound playful; too odd a word to land as a real charge.

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The adverb of *terrible*: blunt and total - among the strongest everyday condemnations.

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Damns by middling - not bad enough to condemn, not good enough to praise.
examples: there have been good and mediocre and bad artists
a mediocre film that nobody remembers

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The adverb of *cursory*: formal and cool - it reports the shallowness without raising its voice.
examples: he looked cursorily through the magazine

entries.definition: conspicuously and offensively loud; given to vehement outcry
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: A crowd word - many voices at once, insisting on something.

entries.definition: very thin especially from disease or hunger or cold
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Thin and worn out - exhaustion showing in the face.

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The adverb of *slick*: the deception is in the smoothness - nothing catches, which is what makes it suspect.

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The formal way of saying nosy, and it grants that curiosity itself was fine.

entries.definition: resembling a beast; showing lack of human sensibility
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: *Brute force* - unreasoning rather than wicked.

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The adverb of *crafty*: homely and old, and the craft is entirely in the deceiving.
examples: he craftily arranged to be there when the decision was announced

entries.definition: devouring or craving food in great quantities
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Appetite as plunder - it has left the table and taken to taking.

entries.label: positive
entries.tone: The adverb of *inquisitive*: praise for a child, and a hint of too many questions for an adult.

entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Gleeful and slightly comic - coined by Lewis Carroll.

entries.label: positive
entries.tone: The adverb of *curious*: approving of the mind and faintly wary of the manner - the gloss admits both.

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The adverb of *piggish*: the same comparison, and the commoner of the two insults.
examples: piggishly, he took two pieces of cake

entries.label: positive
entries.tone: The British spelling of the same funeral-shaped praise.

entries.definition: with a lack of courage and determination
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The adverb of *pusillanimous*: bookish contempt - small-spirited in the face of difficulty.

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: *Don't get cute with me* - charm deployed as a manoeuvre.
examples: a child with intolerably cute mannerisms

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Loud and undignified, but not unkind - the word for a child's full-throated crying.
examples: The baby bawled the entire flight.

entries.definition: characterized by strictness, severity, or restraint
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Neutral in the balance - a strict teacher is a complaint or a compliment depending on the year.

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Attacks the sound and the character together - it says the complaint is beneath answering.

entries.label: positive
entries.tone: A letter-opening formula for the most part, and emptied by that use.

entries.definition: having or showing arrogant superiority to and disdain of those one views as unworthy
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Cold, distant superiority - looking down from a height.

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Commercial - the boasting is on behalf of something being sold.

entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Scottish and northern English warmth - healthy and pleasing.

entries.label: positive
entries.tone: The adverb of *excellent*: unqualified praise - at the top of its class.

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Blunter and more childish than boast; the word itself is faintly playground.

entries.definition: shed tears because of sadness, rage, or pain
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Dignified and literary - grief that deserves respect.
examples: The girl in the wheelchair wept with frustration when she could not get up the stairs

entries.definition: petty or reluctant in giving or spending
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The money was given - resentfully, which is what makes it worse than refusal for some.

entries.definition: say something to someone that expresses praise
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Small, direct and social - one remark, given to a person's face.
examples: He complimented her on her last physics paper

entries.definition: pass from physical life and lose all bodily attributes and functions necessary to sustain life
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: The standard gentle phrase - what you say to someone who has just lost a person.
examples: I'm so sorry - when did she pass away?

entries.definition: pass from physical life and lose all bodily attributes and functions necessary to sustain life
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Casual to the point of dismissive.

entries.definition: thickly covered with ingrained dirt or soot
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Informal and unimpressed, though a whole music scene wore it as a badge.

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The adverb of *clamorous*: a crowd word - many voices at once, insisting on something.

entries.definition: marked by or given to doubt
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: A vice socially and a virtue scientifically; the field decides the charge.

entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Loyalty proved over time, and in Britain it also means Conservative.
examples: a reliable true-blue country club conservative

entries.label: positive
entries.tone: The adverb of *genteel*: faintly pitying since the nineteenth century - shabby-genteel is never far away.
examples: the English lived genteelly in India

entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Chivalrous courage - noble and old-fashioned.
examples: put up a gallant resistance to the attackers

entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Formal and considering; the eyes are doing the work of the mind.

entries.definition: express that something is worthy of praise
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Public by nature - the praise is performed so that others see it given.

entries.definition: having or showing keen interest or intense desire or impatient expectancy
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Warm and forward-looking; the desire is presented as a credit to the person.
